title: A 6.78MHz 94.2% Peak Efficiency Class-E Transmitter with Adaptive Real-Part Impedance Matching and Imaginary-Part Phase Compensation Achieving a 33W Wireless-Power-Transfer System
problem: Wireless power transfer (WPT) systems achieve high efficiency only at specific load points; load impedance varies significantly as charging state changes, causing both real and imaginary parts to shift beyond the circuit's operating range.
motivation: Wide-range impedance matching is critical for practical WPT systems that must charge devices with varying load conditions (battery SOC, temperature, coil coupling distance).
method: A 6.78MHz Class-E power amplifier (a highly efficient power circuit) solves wireless charging efficiency by separately controlling how the circuit adapts to changing loads. It adjusts the real part of load impedance (the resistive load) using a dynamic matching network, and adjusts the imaginary part (the phase shift) using adaptive capacitance, specifically using tunable elements instead of nonlinear MOS capacitors. This dual control keeps the circuit operating efficiently across changing charge states, achieving 94.2% peak efficiency.
key_novelty: Separately controlling the real and imaginary parts of load impedance with adaptive tuning elements instead of using nonlinear MOS capacitors.
